title: Compatible internal bar columns and the total augmentation
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative condensed ring on the small coherent site of profinite sets [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, def-weil-size-convention], and let $G$ be a profinite group (compact Hausdorff and an inverse limit of finite discrete groups), with $\underline G(S)=C(S,G)$. Write $\mathcal M_A$ for internal $A$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] and $\mathcal E_A$ for modules with $A$-linear $\underline G$-action and equivariant maps [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. Let $U:\mathcal E_A\to\mathcal M_A$ forget the action and $\Gamma_G$ take the invariant submodule, fixed after every profinite base change. For a profinite parameter $S$, $A[S]$ is the free internal module on its representable condensed set; $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A$ is internal module Hom, right adjoint to tensor. Use the internal bar diagrams of [def-sfb-condensed-equivariant-bar-data]. Suppose $\mathcal E_A,\mathcal M_A$ are Grothendieck abelian, $U$ is exact and preserves injectives, and the invariant functor is left exact. Let $a:N[0]\to I^\bullet$ be a nonnegative equivariant injective resolution [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. For $p,q\ge0$ put
$$D(I)^{p,q}=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(A[\underline G^p],UI^q),$$
zero otherwise. Give it the inhomogeneous bar differential horizontally and the resolution differential vertically. Assume each augmented horizontal row $0\to\Gamma_G(I^q)\to D(I)^{0,q}\to D(I)^{1,q}\to\cdots$ is exact. Then the two differentials commute, and all columns of this one double complex simultaneously represent $R\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(A[\underline G^p],UN[0])$, including the entire cosimplicial diagram and its first action faces. The derived internal Hom is derived in its second variable; the comparisons are the canonical derived-unit comparisons [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. For the finite-diagonal total [def-sp-double-complex-total] with differential $d_h+(-1)^p d_I$, the map
$$b_I:\Gamma_G(I^\bullet)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Tot}D(I)$$
given in degree $q$ by invariant inclusion into $D(I)^{0,q}$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Thus $Q(b_I):Q\Gamma_G(I^\bullet)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q\operatorname{Tot}D(I)$ is an isomorphism in the ordinary derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], where $Q$ denotes localization. The interchange of the two indices identifies the two total sign conventions by multiplication by $(-1)^{pq}$ in bidegree $(p,q)$; each degree-$n$ total uses only $n+1$ summands. This assertion is about a specified resolution and its actual augmentation map.

proof.text: For each $p\geq0$ write $H_p(M)=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(A[\underline G^p],M)$ and $B_p=H_pU$. The bar data give a cosimplicial diagram of additive functors $B_p:\mathcal E_A\to\mathcal M_A$. Postcomposition by an equivariant map $f$ commutes with every face and degeneracy: for the first face the required equality is $f(g\cdot x)=g\cdot f(x)$; for the other faces and degeneracies it is equality of postcomposition with substitution of parameters. These equalities hold after every profinite base change. Apply them to $d_I^q$. Each cosimplicial operator is then a map of vertical complexes, so its alternating sum $d_h$ commutes with $d_I$. The cosimplicial identities give $d_h^2=0$, and $d_I^2=0$ since $I$ is a complex. Thus this is one commuting first-quadrant double complex, including the first action faces.

source.place: Paragraph (3), internal-bar expansion: the specified cosimplicial diagram and its equivariant first face.

proof.text: Exactness of $U$ implies $H^q(UI)=U(H^q(I))$: it preserves the kernels and images defining cohomology. Hence $Ua:UN[0]\to UI$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Its terms are injective by the assumed preservation of injectives, and it is zero in negative degrees. By [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective], both $I$ in $\mathcal E_A$ and $UI$ in $\mathcal M_A$ are K-injective. The Grothendieck hypotheses and [lem-pur-kinjective-degreewise-existence] supply K-injective resolutions of all complexes in both categories, so the total right derived functors of the additive $H_p$ and $B_p$ exist as in [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. Additivity here is just postcomposition: $H_p(f+g)(u)=fu+gu$. No exactness of $H_p$ or projectivity of $A[\underline G^p]$ is needed.

Let $\eta^p$ be the unit for $RH_p$ and $\zeta^p$ the unit for $RB_p$. The canonical computation maps are
$$c_p=(\eta^p_{UI})^{-1}RH_p(Q(Ua)):RH_p(QUN[0])\xrightarrow{\sim}QH_p(UI),$$
$$e_p=(\zeta^p_I)^{-1}RB_p(Qa):RB_p(QN[0])\xrightarrow{\sim}QB_p(I).$$
Every factor is invertible: the units on K-injectives by [def-sfb-right-derived-functor], and the images of $Ua,a$ because localization inverts quasi-isomorphisms. Both right-hand objects are exactly the localization of the same column $D(I)^{p,\bullet}$, not merely objects with isomorphic cohomology. This proves the asserted second-variable derived internal-Hom column computation with its specified unit normalization.

source.place: Tag 070Y, lemma-K-injective-defined; canonical comparison obtained by applying the unit to the specified resolution.

proof.text:
For any cosimplicial operator $\alpha:B_p\Rightarrow B_r$, the universal property in [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] gives the unique $R\alpha:RB_p\Rightarrow RB_r$ satisfying
$$(R\alpha\,Q)\zeta^p=\zeta^r\,Q\alpha.$$
Indeed the right side is a natural transformation $QB_p\to RB_rQ$, precisely the input to that bijection. The identity transformation and the composite of two such transformations satisfy the corresponding equation, so uniqueness gives $R(1)=1$ and $R(\beta\alpha)=R\beta\,R\alpha$. Thus every cosimplicial relation is retained. This construction is on $\mathcal E_A$: the first action face is a natural transformation there by Step 1, so it is included in exactly the same equation.

source.place: Paragraph (3), internal-bar expansion: compatible derived columns; elementary application of the displayed universal property of the derived unit.

proof.text:
Naturality of $R\alpha$ at $Qa$ and the equation of Step 4 at $I$ give, with right-to-left composition,
$$e_r(R\alpha)_{QN[0]}=Q(\alpha_I)e_p.$$
Explicitly, substitute $e_r=(\zeta^r_I)^{-1}RB_r(Qa)$, move $R\alpha$ past $RB_r(Qa)$ by naturality, and use $(\zeta^r_I)^{-1}(R\alpha)_{QI}=Q(\alpha_I)(\zeta^p_I)^{-1}$. Identify $RB_p(QN[0])$ with $RH_p(QUN[0])$ by $c_p^{-1}e_p$. The displayed equality then says that $c_p$ identifies the whole derived cosimplicial diagram with the columns and actual cosimplicial operators on this single $D(I)$. It applies to all first faces as well as the parameter-substitution faces and degeneracies. It involves no independently chosen column resolutions.

source.place: Paragraph (3), internal-bar expansion: derived-unit normalization on the same resolution; equation for every cosimplicial operator.

proof.text: Put $C^q=\Gamma_G(I^q)$, with differential induced by $d_I$. Equivariance of $d_I$ implies $d_I(\Gamma_GI^q)\subseteq\Gamma_GI^{q+1}$. Let $i:C\to D(I)^{0,\bullet}$ be the invariant inclusion. It commutes with vertical differentials. The horizontal differential on bar degree zero is $x\mapsto(g\mapsto g\cdot x-x)$, so $d_hi=0$, including for generalized sections after base change. The total differential on bar degree zero has vertical sign $+1$. Therefore the prescribed $b_I$, obtained from $i^q$ by the $(0,q)$ coprojection, is a chain map into the total of [def-sp-double-complex-total].

source.place: Paragraph (3), internal-bar expansion: actual invariant augmentation into bar degree zero.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-first-quadrant-column-augmentation] in the abelian category $\mathcal M_A$ to $K=D(I)$, $C=\Gamma_G(I)$, $i$ and the actual $b_I$ from Step 6. Both $K$ and $C$ are nonnegative. For each fixed $q$, the row map $C^q[0]\to D(I)^{\bullet,q}$ is a quasi-isomorphism: exactness of the assumed augmented row identifies $C^q$ with the degree-zero kernel and makes every positive row cohomology object zero; the negative degrees vanish. The theorem therefore says that this very $b_I$ is a quasi-isomorphism. By [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], localization sends it to an isomorphism $Q(b_I)$. No row acyclicity theorem for arbitrary condensed actions is asserted or used: exactness of these injective rows is a hypothesis of this item.

source.place: Tag 0133, lemma-double-complex-gives-resolution, variant in the second variable: specified row augmentation.

proof.text: In total degree $n\geq0$, precisely the indices $p=0,\ldots,n$, $q=n-p$ can contribute; for $n<0$ there are none. Thus every total here is a finite biproduct. Transpose the two indices and multiply the $(p,q)$ summand by $s_{p,q}=(-1)^{pq}$. The transposed differential is $d_I+(-1)^q d_h$. For horizontal arrows, $s_{p+1,q}=(-1)^q s_{p,q}$; for vertical arrows, $(-1)^p s_{p,q+1}=s_{p,q}$. These are exactly the two chain-map equations between the two totals. Since $s_{p,q}^2=1$, the map is its own inverse after transposition. It is $1$ on $p=0$, so it preserves the specified augmentation.
